notes:
A reorganised TV interface. Desktop is unchanged in this release - everything below is the 10-foot TV layout.

Home is now its own place. The sidebar gains a Home item above Search, and it is where the app opens. It answers the what-should-I-watch question: Continue Watching, Recommended for You, Recently Added and Top Rated, each one spanning movies, series and anime together rather than being tied to whichever category you were last browsing.

Movies, Series and Anime are now purely for browsing. Each is Popular plus seven genre rows for that category, drawn from its own genre list, so anime keeps its own taxonomy rather than borrowing the movie one. Continue Watching, Recommended, Recently Added and Top Rated no longer appear on all three; they live on Home. That also means opening Movies only fetches movies, which makes it noticeably lighter on a TV box.

My list is now called Library, with the same icon the desktop app uses for it.

Returning from a title keeps your place. Coming back from a title page used to drop you at the top of the page however far down you had scrolled. It now returns you to exactly where you were, with the rows you had already loaded, and puts the focus ring back on screen next to you.

Back now gets you out of the content. On Home, Movies, Series and Anime, pressing Back while you are somewhere in the rows moves focus to the sidebar instead of leaving the page, so there is no more holding Left through a whole row of posters to get out. Up and Down then move through the sidebar, Right takes you back to the exact poster you left, and a second Back leaves the page as it always did. Everywhere else, Back is unchanged.
